_comment: aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --cli-input-json file://asg.json. Replace ASG_NAME, LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_NAME, SUBNET_ID and the instance type list. Strip the _comment keys before use. Create with DesiredCapacity 0 so nothing launches until you cut over, then update to Min=1 Max=1 Desired=1.
_comment_size: Min=Max=Desired=1 after cutover. Max MUST be 1: a non-Multi-Attach EBS volume attaches to exactly one instance, so two instances would fight over it (and, for a chat gateway, would open two connections on the same bot token). The cost of Max=1 is that a replacement cannot launch until the old instance is gone, so expect a 2-4 minute gap per interruption. That gap is inherent to single-volume designs, not a bug.
_comment_az: ONE subnet only, in the same AZ as the data volume. Listing more subnets would let the ASG launch in an AZ where the volume cannot be attached.
_comment_health: EC2 health checks are instance-level, not application-level. A booted-but-broken app looks healthy here; that gap is covered by kirocrew-selfheal.service plus the CloudWatch alarm.

LaunchTemplate._comment_overrides: All entries must share the AMI's architecture and have enough memory for the workload. More types = more capacity pools = faster recovery. Burstable (t3/t3a) types are included as a fallback but will throttle a sustained-CPU workload once credits run out.

InstancesDistribution._comment_spot: 100% spot. There is no automatic spot-to-on-demand fallback in an ASG; if you need one you must set OnDemandBaseCapacity to 1, which for a single-instance workload means paying on-demand permanently.
